sources.title: EV Database - Hyundai IONIQ 6 Long Range 2WD (MY23-25)
sources.notes: European car: 77.4 kWh nominal, 74.0 kWh usable (estimated by EVDB), NMC, 697 V, max DC 233 kW, AC 11 kW, 10-80 % 17 min (Hyundai claims 18).

sources.title: EV Database - Hyundai IONIQ 6 Standard Range 2WD (MY23-25)
sources.notes: European car: 53.0 kWh nominal, 50.0 kWh usable, NMC, 480 V nominal, max DC 150 kW, AC 11 kW, 10-80 % 18 min.

sources.title: EV Database - Hyundai IONIQ 6 N (MY26)
sources.notes: European car: 84.0 kWh nominal, 80.0 kWh usable (estimated by EVDB), NMC, 697 V, max DC 263 kW, AC 11 kW, 10-80 % 18 min.

sources.title: Hyundai Motor Company newsroom - 2023 IONIQ 6 leads new era of electrification at 2022 Automobility Los Angeles (US spec)
sources.notes: US-spec 2023 IONIQ 6: 77.4 kWh pack, 10.9 kW onboard charger, 10-80 % about 18 min on a 350 kW charger; battery heater warms the pack before fast charging, starts automatically when a charging stop is entered in navigation, or manually via the MyHyundai app while plugged in. Does not give a DC peak kW, usable kWh or the port type.

sources.title: Hyundai owner's manual (CE1, 2024, en_US) - Setting Electric Vehicle Specialized Functions
sources.notes: CE1 is the IONIQ 6 manual code (page does not name the model): Battery Conditioning Mode optimises battery temperature when a DC charging station is set as destination, and can be turned on manually from EV Settings.

sources.title: Hyundai owner's manual (CE1, 2025, en_US) - Setting Electric Vehicle Specialized Functions
sources.notes: CE1 is the IONIQ 6 manual code (page does not name the model): navigation trigger (DC station as destination) plus manual Battery Conditioning Mode in EV Settings.

sources.title: Hyundai Owners (US) - NACS adapter giveaway FAQs
sources.notes: Free CCS-to-NACS adapter for Hyundai EVs with native CCS ports: KONA Electric (no year given), IONIQ 5 22MY-24MY, IONIQ 6 22MY-25MY; vehicle retail date on or before 2025-01-31; later buyers can buy the adapter from dealers.

sources.title: Electrek - Hyundai shaking up 2027 EV lineup: what is changing (2026-11-11)
sources.notes: 2027 IONIQ 6 N: 84 kWh, 10-80 % in about 18 min on a 350 kW charger, native NACS port; standard IONIQ 6 discontinued in the US.

sources.title: Hyundai UK - IONIQ 6 N range and charging
sources.notes: UK page: 84 kWh battery, 350 kW charging with footnote that the car accepts up to 240 kW in optimal conditions; upgraded coolant heater and thermal management shorten battery conditioning time.

sources.title: CarExpert (Australia) - Hyundai IONIQ 6 N (2027) price and specs
sources.notes: Australian car: 84 kWh (gross/usable not stated), DC up to 260 kW, AC up to 10.5 kW (onboard charger), 10-80 % about 0.3 h.

sources.title: The Weekly Driver - Hyundai/Kia pre-E-GMP 64 kWh battery (Kona Electric 2019-2023)
sources.notes: 64 kWh pack, NCM 622, 356 V (3P98S), LG Chem pouch cells, 77 kW DC peak, 7.2 kW AC, 2019-2023 Kona Electric.

sources.title: EV Database - Hyundai Kona Electric 64 kWh (MY20-21)
sources.notes: European car: 64.0 kWh usable, 67.5 kWh nominal, 77 kW max DC via CCS, 11 kW AC (three-phase, EU).

sources.title: EV Database - Hyundai Kona Electric 64 kWh (MY22-23)
sources.notes: European car, same 64 kWh pack: 64.0 kWh usable, 67.5 nominal, up to 77 kW DC; lists battery preconditioning as not supported.

sources.title: xautoworld - 2019 Hyundai Kona Electric (relays Hyundai US press release)
sources.notes: Relays Hyundai US launch material: 64 kWh pack, 7.2 kW Level II onboard charger, 100 kW DC fast charging standard (0-80 % about 54 min at 100 kW), SAE Combo port.

sources.title: EV Specifications - 2024 Hyundai KONA Electric (North America) comparison
sources.notes: NA 2024 Kona Electric: NCM (NMC) chemistry; SE 48.6 kWh 269 V, SEL/Limited 64.8 kWh 358 V; 10.8 kW onboard AC; DC max listed as 100 kW for all three (gross/usable not said).

sources.title: The Weekly Driver - Hyundai Kona EV 64.8 kWh battery
sources.notes: 64.8 kWh, 358 V, CATL cells, 100 kW peak, 10.8 kW AC, battery heating on all trims.

sources.title: EV Database - Hyundai Kona Electric 48 kWh (MY24-25)
sources.notes: European car: 51.0 kWh nominal, 48.4 kWh usable, 295 V, max DC 75 kW, 43 min 10-80 % (Hyundai claims 41), 11 kW AC.

sources.title: EV Database - Hyundai Kona Electric 65 kWh (MY24-25)
sources.notes: European car: 65.4 kWh usable, 68.5 kWh nominal, 400 V, max DC 105 kW, 11 kW AC, preconditioning supported.

sources.title: Hyundai UK - KONA Electric performance and range
sources.notes: UK page: 65.4 kWh long-range battery, 102 kW DC rapid charger, 10-80 % in 41 min, 10.5 kW onboard charger, battery pre-conditioning when navigating to a charger.

sources.title: Hyundai owner's manual (SX2EV, 2025, en_US) - Setting Electric Vehicle Specialized Functions
sources.notes: Page does not name the model; assumed to be the Kona Electric (SX2) manual from its code. Battery Conditioning operates automatically when a DC charging station is set as destination or waypoint, and can be activated manually from the infotainment menu.

sources.title: Electric Revs - Exclusive details on Hyundai's new battery thermal management design (2018-12-20)
sources.notes: 2019 Kona Electric: Canadian cars have a 2 kW battery heater and heat pump, US cars no battery heater; Winter Mode warms the pack for quicker DC charging. Also InsideEVs https://insideevs.com/news/341712/hyundai-kona-electric-thermal-management-system-explained/ (US cars lack active battery heating).

battery.capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 74.0 kWh usable (itself an estimate) for the 77.4 kWh European IONIQ 6 Long Range (MY23-25), same pack and generation. Compared 2023-2025 (pre-facelift first generation, same E-GMP 77.4 kWh pack/charger; Hyundai US 2023 launch release, EVDB MY23-25 entry, Hyundai US 2024/2025 manuals).

battery.chemistry.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists an NMC cathode for the same 77.4 kWh pack (European MY23-25).

battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: Hyundai: 800 V architecture; EVDB lists 697 V nominal for the pack. Class read from the 800 V architecture claim (page cites 350 kW charging).

battery.preconditioning.notes: Hyundai LA press release for the US-spec 2023 car: battery heater starts automatically when a charging stop is entered in navigation, or manually via the MyHyundai app while plugged in. (Green Car Reports at launch said no in-car manual button; the app control counts as the manual control.)

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists max DC 233 kW for the European 77.4 kWh IONIQ 6 (MY23-25); Wikipedia infobox also 233 kW. Hyundai itself only states 18 min on a 350 kW charger. Same pack, same generation.

ac_max_kw.notes: US-spec 2023 IONIQ 6 standard 10.9 kW onboard charger (EV Database lists 11 kW for the European car). Applied to the Canadian cars and later years: nothing found that shows a different charger.

published_10_80_min.notes: About 18 minutes from 10 to 80 % on a 350 kW charger at optimal battery temperature (Hyundai US launch release).

charge_port.notes: Hyundai US lists the IONIQ 6 (22MY-25MY) among EVs with native CCS ports eligible for the CCS-to-NACS adapter.

supercharger_access.notes: Free adapter (retail date on or before 2025-01-31, offer ended 2025-05-30) and dealer-sold adapter afterwards: an owner can use Tesla Superchargers through the CCS-to-NACS adapter.
